They were hard and disobedient, living a detestable and most unlawful life. God, the manager of all things, after a blow and scourges and the things that happened to them from enemies at times, and of the most pleasant things and knowing how to delight, makes the proclamation. He promises that he will also bring back those who have already been taken captive, and will free them from the bonds of their affliction, and will deliver those who previously conquered into the hands of enemies. For it was likely, if they remained unmoved towards those things, but now they would choose even to be envied by the second, and being lifted up into hope of the things they desired, to honor the most beloved service to God, and to keep their mind unwavering towards Him. Since, therefore, many had invaded the land of the Jews at times, but the Chaldeans, who were more savage and wild, and those who ruled Babylon at times, were the first to be spoken to by the word of prophecy, which says: 'On a bare mountain, raise a sign.' It seems to me that it is necessary to make an accurate interpretation of the things that have been said, and to have made a choice of the most necessary things. Cyrus, therefore, who was the son of Cambyses and the father of Mandane, and who ruled over the Persians and Medes, made war against Babylon, and against the whole land of the Chaldeans, which was large and very extensive; and he prevailed.

He took it not by his own powers, nor by a stronger hand, for the Chaldean nation was unconquerable and unopposed due to its multitude and well-trained tactics, but rather God allowed him to overcome those who opposed him and to subdue the impiety of the Babylonians; for the most part, sorcery was prevalent among them; the number of idols was greater; and the land was named after the idols, either due to their multitude or because each of the inhabitants had not refrained from idols in any way, but rather had given themselves over to error without restraint; then, in addition to these things, they had desecrated the holy and consecrated land, that is, Judaea, and had burned Jerusalem and the divine temple, and had taken the sacred vessels to their own land, and in uncontrolled anger had slaughtered the Israelites, a holy people, a portion and inheritance of God; for it is not unclear to those who know the sacred scriptures that God handed over the idolatrous Israel to the hands of enemies, and they were not punished moderately
pass_b_english: The people were stubborn and disobedient, leading a life that was detestable and utterly contrary to the law.
God, who manages all things, had allowed them to suffer a blow and be scourged by their enemies, and had given them a taste of the most pleasant things, but they had not responded.

Now, God makes a proclamation, promising that He will bring back those who have already been taken captive and will free them from the bonds of their affliction, and will deliver those who previously conquered into the hands of enemies.

It was likely that, even if they had remained unmoved by those things, they would now choose to be envied by others, and would be lifted up into hope of the things they desired, and would honor the most beloved service to God, and keep their mind unwavering towards Him.

Many had invaded the land of the Jews at various times, but the Chaldeans, who were more savage and wild, and those who ruled Babylon, were the first to be spoken to by the word of prophecy, which says, 'Raise a sign on a bare mountain' (Isaiah 13:2).

Cyrus, the son of Cambyses and the father of Mandane, who ruled over the Persians and Medes, made war against Babylon and the whole land of the Chaldeans, which was large and very extensive, and he prevailed.
It seems that the interpretation of these events is necessary to understand the choices that were made, and to have made a choice of the most necessary things.
The Chaldean nation was not conquered by human strength or military might, for it was unconquerable and unopposed due to its multitude and well-trained tactics.

However, God allowed the conqueror to overcome those who opposed him and to subdue the impiety of the Babylonians, for the most part, sorcery was prevalent among them, and the number of idols was greater.

In fact, the land was even named after these idols, either due to their multitude or because each of the inhabitants had given themselves over to idolatry without restraint, succumbing to error without control.
Furthermore, the Babylonians had desecrated the holy land of Judaea, burning Jerusalem and the divine temple, and taking the sacred vessels to their own land.
In their uncontrolled anger, they slaughtered the Israelites, a holy people and a portion of God's inheritance.
This was not a surprise to those familiar with the sacred scriptures, for it is clear that God handed over the idolatrous Israel to the hands of their enemies, and they were not punished lightly.
